what_this_is: The cv04 measurement envelope the slab-family consumers derive their windows from. EVIDENCE, not a gate: the gate is round-up(value * multiplier) at the consumer's quantum (tests/_gate_policy.py), computed from these values and written down nowhere else. Revisions are append-only and, once written, immutable; a consumer moves only when its own adoption record is edited and reviewed.

r1.witness_note: No rig-variation sibling exists for these values: the run-length and mesh 2x checks that methodology section 3.2 requires of a user-visible number were NOT run as sibling artifacts on this rung. The source comment records that widening to nx=1500 / 1940 steps collapses the per-bin closure to 0.0002, and the case's own claim_scope records that more than half of mean_dT is record truncation at this rung -- both are prose, neither is a committed sibling artifact. These values are CARRIED, not witnessed.

per_bin_max_RT_closure.previous_home_quote: max|R+T-1| = 0.0487, worst bin at the 11.87 GHz mask edge

observables.mean_dR: arithmetic mean over the masked bins of |R_rfx(f) - R_tmm(f)|
observables.mean_dT: arithmetic mean over the masked bins of |T_rfx(f) - T_tmm(f)|
observables.mean_closure: arithmetic mean over the masked bins of |R_rfx(f) + T_rfx(f) - 1|
observables.per_bin_max_RT_closure: max over the masked bins of |R_rfx(f) + T_rfx(f) - 1|

measurement_identity.units: absolute power ratio (R, T and their sum are dimensionless powers); every value is an absolute, not relative, difference
measurement_identity.normalization: R = |FFT(E_total - E_inc, refl probe)|^2 / |FFT(E_inc, refl probe)|^2 and T = |FFT(E_total, trans probe)|^2 / |FFT(E_inc, trans probe)|^2, each bin normalized by the SAME run's 1-D auxiliary incident field at the same x (TFSF two-grid), so no separate reference run enters.
measurement_identity.frequency_mask: 3 GHz < f < 15 GHz AND incident |FFT| > 0.02 of its own peak, on the rFFT grid of the 719-step record zero-padded by nfft_oversample = 8. The mask is the evaluated band; the consumers' 4-10 GHz gated band is a SUBSET declared by the consumers, not by this artifact.
measurement_identity.reference: exact normal-incidence transfer-matrix (Fresnel) R, T of the same slab; no external solver enters these four values
measurement_identity.extraction_convention: single-run TFSF, scattered field at the reflection probe by subtracting the 1-D incident, total field at the transmission probe; power ratios, magnitudes only (no phase); float32 fields (jax_x64 false).

raw_data_identity.note: The C4 rung's per-bin R(f)/T(f) arrays are NOT committed anywhere in this repository: cv04 writes plots and a fringe-gate/lattice-witness record, not its own R/T arrays. These four scalars are therefore the narrowest committed form of this measurement, which is exactly why they were being copied into consumer modules and UI fixtures. Recording that gap here is part of the evidence.

measurement_identity.processing_revision: cv04 as committed at the C4 rung: mean gates and the per-bin closure ceiling of issue #341; the fringe gate (#812) and the lattice witness (2026-09-03) were added later and do not change these four values

lattice_identification.claim: the adopted mean_dR is dominated by this slab's Yee-lattice second-order term, not by solver error (cv04 claim_scope, 2026-09-03 lattice-witness standard); mean_dT at this rung is dominated by RECORD TRUNCATION and the identification does NOT cover it

rfx_vs_lattice_mean_dR_gated.means: |R_rfx - R_lattice| in the gated mean at THIS rung; the adopted envelope 0.0066 is |R_rfx - R_transfer_matrix|

rfx_vs_lattice_mean_dT_gated.means: the same for T; 0.0063 of the 0.011 T envelope is this rung's record truncation, which is why W_MEAN_T is not a discretisation number

witness_gated_here.means: false: at this rung the derived W_witness exceeds cv04's own band-mean window, so the lattice witness is REPORTED, not gated

settled_sibling_rung.means: the same rig SETTLED (1067 steps, cv23's lossy arm): |rfx - lattice| is 43x inside its own witness window, which is the shape cv04's rung would take if it settled

lattice_identification.nulls: The '~100 % lattice fraction' and the 5.3e-06 gated settling residual quoted in the issue #928 discussion are NOT in any tracked artifact under those definitions: _23_lossy_results/lattice_witness.json has no sigma_zero rung (its rungs are the three lossy arms and their dx ladders), and cv04's own lattice witness stores per-bin arrays plus the gated means above, no fraction and no settling residual. They are written null rather than typed in from the discussion. Producing them is a measurement change (a settled cv04 rung), i.e. revision r2 in its own PR.

rig.record_length_law: cv04 CPML round-trip rule: v_cells = c0*dt/dx; n_steps = min(int(2*dist_to_cpml_hi/v_cells*0.95), int(2*dist_to_cpml_lo/v_cells*0.95), 8000), the probes 30 cells either side of the slab. NOT the ring-down (-40 dB) law cv22/cv23 derive for their own records.

notes: dt_s is the committed run's own timestep, read from _04_fresnel_results/lattice_witness.json::rungs.slab_eps4.dt_s (and identical in fringe_gate_geometry.json::config.dt_s), both artifacts of this case. It was null in the first draft of this file on the argument that no artifact carried it; the argument was wrong (PR review, 2026-09-06), and the same standard that fills n_steps / nx_interior / n_cpml fills it.

code_sha is null: the C4 rung's job id is recorded in the cv04 source comment and in the cv22 pre-declaration, but no committed file carries the commit it was built from. gallery_snapshot_git_sha belongs to a DIFFERENT run (the 1.6.5 gallery precompute) that reports the same three band-mean values; it is a second home for the values, not this run's commit.

rig_provenance says, per key, whether the value is attested by a committed run snapshot (gallery-manifest) or only declared by the committed producer script (cv04-source). Nothing here is read from today's library defaults.
The rig is the PRODUCER's. cv22 and cv23 run their own record-length recipe on the same grid and TFSF; that is a consumer property and is not described here.

Adopting different evidence -- for example cv04 re-run with the corrected injection plane, where the per-bin closure is reported as 0.0043 -- is a NEW revision plus an edit to each consumer's adoption record, in a PR that says so. It is never a consequence of re-running the producer.

The revision block holds the measurement and the configuration that produced it, and nothing about who cites it: `adopted_by` used to live inside it, so a third adopter would have changed revision_hash on a merged revision and broken both existing consumers' pins. The rig_provenance legend moved out for the same reason -- it is a key to the artifact's vocabulary, not part of the measurement. This is the LAST bootstrap-time re-stamp of r1: from here the immutability rule is what applies.

rig_provenance_keys.cv04-artifact: read out of validation/crossval/_04_fresnel_results/lattice_witness.json::rungs.slab_eps4 (and identical in fringe_gate_geometry.json::config)
rig_provenance_keys.cv04-source: declared by the committed producer script; no run artifact attests it

adoption: Adoption is declared in the CONSUMER, never here. A consumer names this artifact, the revision it adopted, that revision's hash, the realized rig's hash and the gate policy it was adopted under; tests/contracts/test_calibration_envelope_ownership.py discovers the adopters by enumerating those declarations. Recording them here would put a third adopter's arrival inside the hashed block, changing revision_hash for a merged revision and invalidating every existing consumer's pin (PR review, round 2).
